coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 5 units, 33 files — matches the expected count exactly. Units are the domain root directory plus the four sub-domain directories (06.01, 06.02, 06.03, 06.04); the seven root-level leaf features 06.05-06.11 belong to the domain-root unit. Every one of the 33 files was read. The six largest leaf files (06.01.01-04, 06.02.01-03, 06.03.02) were read in full, line-numbered. For the remaining large files the 'Deep Think Annotations' rationale essays and the auto-generated 'Related Specs' link blocks were read with per-cell truncation (the DT verdict, source and decision-bearing opening of every row was read in full; only the trailing argumentation prose was elided) — every Overview, Role Lens, Behavior, Happy Path, Edge Case table, States table, Cross-Cut Notes, Decisions table and Open Questions table in the domain was read verbatim. The domain CX (428 lines) was read by structural extraction: all headings, the full Cross-Cut Map table, every Relationship/Role-scoping/Synthesis line and every marker line, plus the full Rejected Pairs table; the per-CX 'Synthesis questions answered' prose for the eight High-confidence entries was not read line-by-line. Scoring notes: dimension 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A for the four sub-domain units because success criteria and competitor analysis live in meta/ (outside these units); both are scored at the domain-root unit, where the index Overview names four competitors with a specific capability gap and a defensible moat, and where the domain's two strategic claims are asserted. Dimension 4 is scored as applicable throughout because these files carry explicit numeric 'Tunable defaults' / weight tables with values, ranges and owners. One finding class recurs across units — inline '[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5]' markers pointing at a stage the tree itself repeatedly describes as completed, with no owner. It is reported once for 06.01 (where it also contradicts a ratified decision), once for 06.03 (where it also contradicts a RESOLVED question) and once for the domain root (where two instances have neither owner nor target). The equivalent instance in 06.02 (CX-05) is not separately reported to avoid padding. This tree is unusually rigorous; most candidate findings were refuted on the devil's-advocate pass and dropped (stale but harmless sibling-Q citations, status-label mismatches between the domain index and two leaf headers, an undefined make-up minimum per cancellation preset, a dangling 'sub-domain D-05' reference in the 06.03 CX, an over-run question cited under the wrong sibling Q-id).

findings.claim: A per-teacher waitlist is ratified as a first-class capability in 06.02.01 (an intake status with a 'Join waitlist' CTA) and appears as the guaranteed floor of 06.02.03's relaxation ladder and as its 'Exhausted' state — while 06.01.01 Q-01 and D-08, and 06.02.03's own D-08/partition-3 row, state that no waitlist node exists anywhere in domain 06 and that a waitlist is new scope requiring /evolve-feature. No file anywhere defines what 'Join waitlist' does: who is notified, when, in what order, whether joining creates any claim on a slot, or how a waitlist entry ends.

findings.forcedInvention: To build the teacher profile page an implementer must invent the entire behaviour behind the 'Join waitlist' CTA — the entry record, the notification trigger, ordering/priority among waiting students, expiry, and whether a waitlisted student gets any precedence when a slot frees — or must decide unilaterally to omit a CTA that 06.02.01 D-05 ratifies. A second, directly conflicting decision is also forced: 06.02.01 renders 'Join waitlist' on a `waitlist`-intake teacher's card while 06.02.03 D-08 requires a fully-booked teacher's card to carry no CTA at all, so the implementer must choose which file governs the same card.
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A reads 06.02.01 D-05 and the Books-closed state and ships a per-teacher waitlist: a 'Join waitlist' button, a waitlist table, and a notification when the teacher reopens intake. Implementer B reads 06.02.03 D-08 and 06.01.01 Q-01, ships no waitlist at all, and renders a fully-booked or waitlist-intake teacher with no CTA and only their next `Completed` series date. Both are faithful to the spec they read. The two builds differ in a database table, a notification pipeline, the primary conversion control on the domain's highest-traffic acquisition page, and whether the relaxation ladder's guaranteed final step ('Never a bare no results') can be honoured at all.

findings.claim: There is no specified way for a student to voluntarily end an ongoing series or to recover money from an unspent pack, yet 06.01.02's own user-facing copy directs them to do exactly that. Refund eligibility is defined only for teacher departure, academy closure, GDPR erasure, chargeback and expiry-to-residual. The series state machine in 06.01.01 has no student-initiated termination state — an ongoing series can only end via Lapsed (non-payment), Completed (fixed-count only) or teacher departure.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent: (a) whether an 'end this series' action exists at all and what it does to the standing slot and to the teacher's notification; (b) whether a voluntary mid-pack refund of unspent credits is granted on request, granted at the teacher's discretion, or refused outright; (c) if granted, whether it refunds cash to the purchaser at the price paid or only converts to redeemable residual; and (d) whether any fee, notice period or teacher consent applies. 06.01.02 Q-01 does not cover this — it is scoped to whether *residual* (which arises only at expiry) is withdrawable as cash, not to live credits held by a student who wants to stop now.
findings.failureScenario: A parent with 6 unspent credits decides after four lessons that the teacher is not a fit and taps the 'request a refund' path 06.01.02 edge case 12 promises them. Implementer A, reading D-04 (expiry degrades to residual, nothing is destroyed) and D-12 (transfer is a departure remedy only), builds no voluntary refund: the parent is told their credits remain with that teacher until the expiry window elapses, then become residual redeemable only against the same teacher they are trying to leave. Implementer B, reading the same edge case's promise that the refund path is 'stated, not hidden', builds a self-service full refund of unspent credits to the purchaser. The two builds differ by the platform's entire prepaid-liability exposure and by whether the copy the spec mandates is true. Separately, the student's Tuesday 17:00 tenancy either persists (nothing ended it) or is released — undefined in both builds.

findings.claim: Two sibling features define the same named state, 'At Risk', on the same entity (the series) with different and non-overlapping triggers: 06.01.01 fires it at a zero balance, 06.01.02 fires it at two or fewer available credits or projected exhaustion within 21 days. Both state the same user-facing consequence (an amber series and a top-up prompt naming the slot's release/funding date), so they are not a warning tier plus a state tier — they are one state with two definitions.

This feature owns the signal and its timing."; 06.01.02-lesson-packages-credits-rate-cards.md:239 — "| At risk | Available ≤ 2, or reserved occurrences exhaust the balance within 21 days | \"Your Tuesday slot is funded to 26 Aug — top up to keep it\" with the specific date, not a percentage |"
findings.failureScenario: A student holds 2 credits against a weekly series. Implementer A follows 06.01.02 and renders the series amber with 'top up to keep it' immediately. Implementer B follows 06.01.01 and D-03 and renders it normally until the balance reaches 0, two lessons later. Because D-03 makes At Risk the state that starts the 2-occurrence / 14-day countdown to Lapsed (tenancy release), the two builds also differ on when the slot-release clock starts — build A releases a non-paying student's standing slot up to two occurrences earlier than build B.

All three 06.04 files and the 06.04 Role Matrix scope the Producer strictly to the author stance, and 06.04.03 gives the Producer Reports-only access — meaning a Producer cannot consume a course. findings.failureScenario: A Producer buys a colleague's mixing course. Implementer A follows 06.04.03's Role Lens and the 06.04 Role Matrix, grants the Producer Reports access only, and the purchased course does not appear in their library — playback is refused for a paid entitlement. Implementer B follows 06.01.02's Role Lens, treats the Producer as a first-class buyer, and grants full consumption. The two builds differ on whether the entitlement check is keyed to the entitlement alone (as 06.04.03 D-05 implies) or additionally gated on persona, and on whether a paying customer is locked out of the product they bought.

findings.claim: The streak mechanic is specified as existing and as 'forgiving by construction' via a freeze/grace allowance, but no value, range or owner is given for that allowance, and no default is stated for whether streaks are on or off. Every comparable knob elsewhere in this domain carries a number, a range and an owner, so the omission is a genuine gap rather than a deliberate deferral: the file's own Q-03 defers only whether the optional streak surface is built at all, not how forgiving it is.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the size and replenishment rule of the freeze/grace allowance (how many missed days a streak absorbs, whether the allowance refills, and over what window), and must invent whether streaks default on or off — and if the default differs for the child student versus the adult self-directed learner that DT-02 says is the segment they fit.
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A gives one grace day per week, so a child practising four days a week keeps an unbroken streak indefinitely. Implementer B gives two grace days total, so the same child's counter shows a gap in week three. D-02's stated purpose — that a lapse renders as a resume point rather than a quit trigger — is met by A and defeated by B, and neither implementer has anything in the spec to check their choice against.

A spec writer drawing the discovery shard has no owner to ask and no stage to defer to, so they either invent the role scoping (deciding unilaterally whether an Operator or a signed-out Fan sees exam-board facets on a minors-facing search surface) or silently drop the cross-cut. The same applies to CX-11's masterclass-to-course bridge, whose object boundary 06.05 Q-03 routes to /create-prd-architecture while the CX itself routes nowhere.

findings.claim: 06.02.04's Role Lens grants the teacher a control to cap how many trials they give per month, but the same file's Behavior section enumerates exactly three ways a trial differs from a normal occurrence and does not include it, and no edge case, state, decision or open question anywhere defines what happens when the cap is reached.
findings.evidence: 06.02.04-trial-lessons-conversion.md:20 — "**As Teacher**: chooses whether to offer trials and at what price (free / reduced / full), caps how many they'll give per month (their time is finite and trials pay badly), sees trial→series conversion"; VERSUS 06.02.04-trial-lessons-conversion.md:27-28 — "A trial is a normal occurrence (06.01.01) with three differences: a trial price, a **one-per-pair cap**, and a conversion moment attached to its end."; the Decisions table at 06.02.04-trial-lessons-conversion.md:104-110 covers price (D-02), the per-pair cap (D-03) and the walk-away (D-04) but carries no monthly cap; the States table at 06.02.04-trial-lessons-conversion.md:67-75 has no cap-exhausted state, only "| Empty | Teacher offers no trials | \"This teacher doesn't offer trials — book a first lesson at {rate}\". Not an error |"
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the cap's period boundary (calendar month or rolling 30 days), whether a booked-but-not-yet-delivered trial consumes the allowance, whether a cancelled trial returns it, and what the student sees on the result card and profile once the month's allowance is spent — the Empty state's copy, a full-rate first lesson, or the teacher disappearing from trial-filtered results altogether.
findings.failureScenario: A teacher sets a cap of four free trials a month and receives four in the first week. Implementer A hides the trial CTA for the rest of the month and falls back to the Empty state's 'book a first lesson at {rate}'. Implementer B keeps the CTA and queues requests past the cap. Implementer C treats the cap as advisory and only reports it. 06.02.03's result cards render 'Free 30-min trial · next Tue 17:00' from this data, so the three builds show three different things on the domain's primary conversion surface.

findings.claim: 06.02.02's Role Lens grants the teacher a private view listing 'what's thin' in their evidence, while the same file's D-03 forbids a completeness nudge for credits and its own edge case forbids ever telling a teacher their profile is incomplete for lacking credits. The two statements cannot both be implemented as written.
findings.evidence: 06.02.02-verified-credentials-credit-backed-credibility.md:34 — "(c) see a private \"what's thin\" view listing evidence they could add."; VERSUS 06.02.02-verified-credentials-credit-backed-credibility.md:305 (D-03) — "| D-03 | Absence of credits is **never** rendered as an absence of trust | ... Operationally: no empty group, no zero count, **no completeness nudge for credits**, and no block at all rather than an empty one. |"; 06.02.02-verified-credentials-credit-backed-credibility.md:210 — "| Excellent teacher, zero verified credits | Block shows qualifications, vouch and vetting; **no penalty, no empty-state shaming** | ... Teacher: never \"your profile is incomplete\" for lacking credits they were never going to have (DT-02) |"; note the narrower, permitted case at 06.02.02-verified-credentials-credit-backed-credibility.md:211 — "Teacher: private view — \"3 credits aren't confirmed yet. Ask someone who was there\"", which is about confirming existing credits rather than about thin evidence
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A builds the 'what's thin' view as described in the Role Lens: a private panel telling a teacher which evidence kinds they are missing. For the solo bedroom producer whose credits are structurally capped below rung 5 forever — a case the file explicitly protects at edge case 212 — that panel is a permanent deficiency marker, which is exactly what D-03 and DT-02 forbid. Implementer B reads D-03 and ships no such view, so the teacher-facing surface promised in the Role Lens does not exist.

findings.claim: The domain's two headline strategic claims and its one stated feature-level success measure are all directional: none carries a number, a unit or a timeframe, so none is falsifiable as written. The domain index resolves that the platform has no measure of learning outcome, but does not substitute any measurable target for the claims it does make.
findings.evidence: education-lessons-mentorship-index.md:13 — "practice tracking is the highest-frequency habit surface in the product — a student opens it daily where an artist opens analytics weekly"; education-lessons-mentorship-index.md:113 (D-08) — "The rationale asserts (a) practice tracking is the product's highest-frequency habit surface and (b) credentialing is the unfair advantage. Drilling **conditionally confirmed (a)**" — with no threshold stated for what would confirm or refute it; 06.03.03-practice-logging-streaks-goals.md:85 (DT-04) — "✅ CONFIRMED, conditionally ... this feature is the strongest candidate on the map" again with no number; and the one explicit success measure, 06.02.03-teacher-discovery-match-criteria.md:308 (D-11) — "The feature's success measure is **search → trial → series conversion**, not click-through or booking" — a named ratio with no target value and no timeframe
findings.failureScenario: Domain 06's own index makes its phase-2 priority contingent on claim (a) — that practice tracking delivers the platform's daily open. With no stated threshold (daily-active rate, sessions per student per week, retention at 90 days), nothing at /plan-phase or after can determine whether the built feature met the claim that justified building it, and D-08's 'conditionally confirmed' condition can never be tested against the shipped product.
